body: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain Oct 26, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Our third lesson in our AI Quests series, “Polar Peaks,” teaches students key AI literacy skills while delving into neuroscience. Ronit Levavi Morad Senior Director, Google Research Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning just launched "Polar Peaks," an interactive quest that teaches students ages 11 to 14 how to map the human brain using artificial intelligence. This program helps students practice data cleaning and model testing while emphasizing the need for human oversight in technology. You can access new teacher training modules through the Google AI Educator Series to help bring these lessons into your classroom. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. "Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain" teaches students how AI works responsibly. Students ages 11 to 14 act as researchers to map neurons and solve mysteries. The game shows how AI helps scientists study the brain and speed up research. New training modules help teachers bring these AI lessons into their classrooms. This award-winning program helps kids learn critical thinking and AI literacy skills. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Google launched a new game called "Polar Peaks" that lets you act like a scientist to map the human brain using AI. You’ll learn how to solve real-world problems while discovering how to use AI responsibly. It’s a fun way to see how researchers use technology to make big scientific breakthroughs. Teachers even get special training to help you explore these challenges in class. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Today, we’re launching “Polar Peaks”, our third quest in the AI Quests series, created by Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning to teach students how AI works and how to use it responsibly. AI Quests invites students ages 11 to 14 to step into the shoes of Google researchers to tackle some of humanity’s biggest challenges. More than 400,000 quests have been completed to date, localized to 10 languages. Alongside the new quest, we’re also releasing training modules for teachers. Polar Peaks: A journey to map the human brain In the first two quests, students tackle flood forecasting and eye disease detection, inspired by Google Research’s Flood Forecasting initiative and AI model for diabetic retinopathy screening. Our newest quest, “Polar Peaks,” has students travel to the frontiers of neuroscience and see how AI can speed up scientific research. With the guidance of in-game mentors, students scan and map the neurons in the brain to better understand the game character’s memory loss. They complete tasks like data cleaning and model testing, learning firsthand that AI requires careful human oversight and critical thinking. The quest is inspired by over a decade of our research in connectomics: the science of mapping neural networks in the brain. Upon completion of the quest, students hear from two researchers behind our real-world breakthroughs, including the recent mapping of the complete fruit fly brain, the largest brain map by number of neurons to date. Related Article 5 amazing visuals of the fruit fly brain Here's how these images are advancing neuroscience. See more Training modules: Tools for teaching AI literacy Teachers play a critical role in bringing the quests to life and fitting them into their existing classroom curriculum. We’re rolling out new dedicated teacher training modules to help educators reinforce key AI literacy concepts and use AI Quests for learning and discussion. These are launching within the Google AI Educator Series . The modules for Quest #1 and #2 are accessible here . The training module for Quest #3 will follow next month. Earlier this year, AI Quests won a 2026 Webby Award for AI Education, Learning & Training, and Best Global K–12 Learning Solution at the ETIH Innovation Awards. We’ll continue working with educators and partners to bring more quests to more classrooms this school year. body: 15 college students share their favorite Gemini features Oct 26, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Here’s how these college students use Gemini to study for exams, organize their notes, knock out projects, and master new material. Lindsey Lanquist Contributor Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Google Student Ambassadors shared 11 ways they use Gemini to study smarter and stay organized. You can use these tools to create custom study guides, practice for interviews with voice chat, and automate your research or scheduling. Try uploading your course materials to Gemini to turn your notes into interactive lessons and quizzes today. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. College students have found all kinds of ways to use Gemini . It helps them learn better, track workouts, turn groceries into tasty meals, vibe-code portfolios — and then review them from a hiring manager’s point of view. So we asked 15 Google Student Ambassadors to share their favorite Gemini features — and how they use them to study smarter, learn faster, produce better work, and stay organized. 1. Study notebooks Study notebooks turn your course materials into personalized, bite-sized lessons. “They make studying more manageable, especially right before finals when I have a semester’s worth of material to review,” says Beverlyn T., University of Southern California. Students use study notebooks for everything from organizing daily coursework to finding themes within their notes. “Study notebooks have made refreshing my memory on 50-page papers before class so much faster,” says Nina R., University of California, Santa Barbara. “And if you upload competing viewpoints, you can quickly generate comparisons and master complex concepts. 2. Gemini Live Gemini Live lets you chat with Gemini using just your voice. “It’s my go-to for practicing interviews and presentations, because it lets me hear how my ideas actually sound,” says Skylar E., San Diego State University. Other students use it to talk through tough concepts on-the-go or practice speaking new languages before studying abroad. You can also turn on your camera to show Gemini Live exactly what you’re looking at. “As a designer, I’m constantly learning new tools and software,” says Debbie C., The University of Texas, Austin. “When I get stuck using one, I can have Gemini Live walk me through it step-by-step.” 3. Guided Learning Guided Learning helps you build understanding instead of just giving you answers. “I paste in my work, and instead of asking for the fix, I let Gemini walk me toward what went wrong,” says Fehmaan K., George Mason University. “It asks me what I think happens at each step, and I usually catch my mistake before it tells me.” Guided Learning asks open-ended questions to probe your understanding. “Resist asking for the answer when you get stuck mid-session,” Fehmaan adds. “Guess even when you’re unsure. Because getting corrected will stick with you more than reading an explanation.” 4. Study guides Gemini can turn your notes into ready-made study guides. “For courses where professors don’t provide exam overviews, this helps me review content and summarize what I need to know,” says Jamie C., University of Southern California. You can upload course materials, like lecture slides or handwritten notes, and tell Gemini what to include. “I recommend dedicating a Google Drive folder to each class you’re taking and sharing that with Gemini,” Jamie adds. “That way, your study guide captures both the professor’s content and your interpretations.” 5. Quizzes Want to check how well you understand a subject? Gemini can generate custom quizzes to help you prep for tests and exams. “Practice quizzes help me build confidence going into high-stakes tests,” says Shuang P., New York University. “Many of my grades depend entirely on exams, so having access to extra practice questions is critical.” When teachers provide practice tests without answer keys, some students use Gemini quizzes to check their work — and understand the logic behind each question. “It helps understand what questions I might miss or misinterpret,” says Tobi U., University of California, Riverside. 6. Unlimited uploads Gemini student plans give you unlimited uploads of class materials, study notebooks, interactive visualizations, and images in general. “This really helps me provide context in my notes,” says Chaeyeon H., Boston University. Say you want to reference something like a homework assignment, lecture slide, historic artifact, or work of art. “Whether it’s a physical object or something on my screen, I can easily snap and upload a photo,” says Nicole F., University of California, San Diego. Other students use the feature before submitting work, uploading their draft and the assignment rubric to double-check that they’ve met every requirement. 7. Audio Overviews With Audio Overviews , you can create podcast-style conversations from documents, slides, and more. “I rely on Audio Overviews to get in last-minute review sessions while walking across campus,” Nina says. “This lets me absorb things conversationally and take active notes while listening.” Students say Audio Overviews are especially handy for more thoroughly exploring class materials and topics. “I like to upload articles with conflicting viewpoints. The hosts naturally argue both sides of the issue,” says Parikshit M., Rutgers University. 8. Image generation Nano Banana , Gemini’s image generator, can help you visualize any idea and design anything. “As a creative, I’ve found image generation models helpful, especially when formatting images and sharpening details,” says Nelson G., Morehouse College. Students are using it outside the classroom, too. “I often get overwhelmed when designing graphics,” Beverlyn says. “I love using Gemini to create club flyers and social media posts. It turns my ideas into eye-catching visuals tailored closely to my style.” 9. Gemini in Chrome With Gemini in Chrome , you can get assistance directly in your browser. “It makes reviewing wrong answers on exams so much more efficient, because I don’t have to copy and paste them into a Gemini chat,” says Megan J., University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. It’s also great for deciphering complex documents. “I can get context without opening a new tab and losing my place,” Fehmaan says. “I recommend using it for ‘What does this specific sentence mean?’ — the narrow questions are where it saves the most time.” 10. Deep Research Deep Research can automatically browse up to hundreds of websites, think through its findings, and create multi-page reports in minutes. Plus, you can talk through the findings on the go with Gemini Live. “It saves me so much time by compiling exhaustive market analyses and literature reviews,” says Annitha K., San Diego State University. “I like to use Gemini to brainstorm a tightly structured research prompt and then feed that into Deep Research.” 11. Connected apps Connecting Gemini to other apps — like Google Drive, Google Calendar, Gmail, and Google Sheets — can help you stay organized. “I have Gemini reference class syllabi in my Drive, find every assignment and due date, and organize them in my Calendar,” Skylar says. “Before winding down, I have Gemini log all my tasks in a master tracking Sheet so I start each morning organized,” says Aaryaman B., Michigan State University. It can also help you stave off inbox chaos. “As a TA for a class, I never want emails from my students to get lost,” Megan says. “Gemini helps me find messages I need to respond to or follow up on, saving time and helping me be a more present educator.” Get the latest news from Google in your inbox Sign up for our newsletters with product updates, event information, special offers, and more. title: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer
body: Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer Oct 26, 2026 | Amy Coleman - Executive Vice President, Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, shared the below communication with Microsoft employees today. Today, we’re introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs. The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program. What employees should know This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below . This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs. Eligible employees will receive an email with a link to their Voluntary Exit Offer details within the next few hours. Looking ahead The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute. My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving. Thank you for everything you continue to do for our customers, Microsoft and for one another. Amy This Viva Engage post has been edited slightly for external use.

title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Amazon Polly Generative engine, TorchNeuron for Trainium, and more (October 26, 2026)
body: AWS Weekly Roundup: Amazon Polly Generative engine, TorchNeuron for Trainium, and more (October 26, 2026) A few weeks ago I presented to a small group of commercial and technology leaders from Brazilian agribusiness at the AWS office in São Paulo. My talk ran through where generative AI fits across the different stages of an agribusiness operation, and the point I kept returning to is that the markets we call traditional are exactly the ones where keeping up with this technology decides who ends up ahead of the curve. Nobody there was arguing about whether AI belongs in agriculture. The questions were about delivery: who receives the output, in which language, on which device, often while driving between farms. That is why a launch I might otherwise have filed under routine leads my list this week. The Amazon Polly Generative engine upgrade added 14 new voices, two of them in Brazilian Portuguese. When your user has both hands on a steering wheel, the interface is a voice. Presenting “GenAI no Agronegócio Brasileiro” at the AWS office in São Paulo. The rest of the week had a sharper edge. The biggest launch is a security service built on the premise that the gap between a vulnerability being disclosed and a vulnerability being exploited has effectively closed, and AWS published the honeypot evidence for exactly that in the same week. Now, let’s get into this week’s AWS news… AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available AWS Continuum reframes vulnerability management as an end-to-end job rather than a scanner that hands you a list. It builds a context graph from your repositories and your AWS environment, assigns each finding an evidence level, and reproduces exploitable findings in an isolated sandbox with proof-of-concept code so you see the issue rather than a severity label. It ranks issues by how close the attack path runs to business-critical systems, then opens the fix as a pull request. The control boundary matters: every remediation currently requires human approval, so you review and merge the pull request, with autonomous classes of fix gated behind confidence thresholds for the future. The “why now” came from AWS’s own honeypots in the same week. Amazon Threat Intelligence found a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt in MadPot telemetry dated October 17, four days before CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 were publicly disclosed, and on disclosure day proof-of-concept exploits were circulating around 02:00 UTC, roughly twelve hours before the embargo was due to lift at 14:00 UTC. The practical reading is direct: a patch window measured in days assumes a delay that no longer exists, and an investigation should start from the earliest known exploitation rather than from the disclosure date. AWS also published the AWS WAF mitigations for the same CVEs. Continuum is available in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon). Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway Amazon ECS Gateway splits the work of exposing a service between the people who own the network and the people who own the application. Platform teams define one gateway with the organization’s subnets, security groups, TLS certificates, listener settings, and AWS WAF web ACLs. Application teams opt in by adding a gateway connector to the service definition, and ECS gives them an ACM certificate, a unique DNS hostname, listener rules, a target group, and a security group that admits traffic only from the Application Load Balancer. The numbers make the economics clear: up to 25 services share a single ALB, ECS provisions the first ALB on first connect and removes ALBs when they are no longer needed, and a gateway can associate with up to 10,000 clusters, with five gateways per cluster. You can adopt it incrementally with UpdateService while your existing load balancer stays in place. Amazon ECS Gateway is available in all commercial Regions where Amazon ECS is available, at no additional charge. Last week’s launches Here are some launches that caught my attention this week. Amazon Polly delivers a major upgrade to its Generative engine – The Generative engine now runs a larger, more expressive catalog: 57 generative voices across 11 languages and 25 locales, with 14 new voices across 9 locales and Hindi and Finnish generally available for the first time. Two of the new voices are Brazilian Portuguese, Leo and Carolina. It is a drop-in upgrade, so the voice names, the same SynthesizeSpeech call, and the price all stay the same while the output gets more natural. AWS announces TorchNeuron: native PyTorch support for AWS Trainium (public beta) – TorchNeuron is an open source PyTorch backend that lets you run your model on Trainium by switching to .to(‘neuron’), a configuration change instead of a rewrite, with eager execution and torch.compile intact. It integrates with the Neuron Kernel Interface for custom operators, and it works on Trainium2 and Trainium3 instances. If you want the bigger picture on why hardware choice should not lock in your software, the AWS Insights piece on that theme is a good companion read, and the release lands alongside AWS Neuron 2.33 . New ways to customize models with Amazon SageMaker AI, without managing GPUs – Training sessions are now generally available, giving you control of the post-training loop, including custom loss functions and reward signals, while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, distributed execution, fault recovery, and checkpoint storage. You pay for the tokens SageMaker AI processes, and the meter stops while your reward function scores a batch. There is a full technical walkthrough , the training session APIs , and new support for Muse Glimmer, Qwen 3.8, and Ministral 3 . Structured outputs for Claude models available on Amazon Bedrock – You can now get schema-compliant JSON back from any Anthropic Claude model on Amazon Bedrock, across both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints, without custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing. That makes jobs like pulling every required field from a financial report, parsing clinical notes, or routing support tickets by intent far more reliable to automate. Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports online migration with zero downtime – You can migrate self-managed Valkey or Redis OSS on Amazon EC2 into ElastiCache Serverless with zero downtime, meaning zero errors returned to the client during the move, measured the way the ElastiCache SLA measures availability. You prepare the migration, start the data sync, then choose a manual or automatic cutover, with no third-party replication tools. It is available in all commercial Regions, the China Regions, and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Other AWS news Here are some additional projects and posts that you might find interesting. Discover tools at runtime with AWS Agent Registry – AWS Agent Registry is a managed catalog for MCP servers, agents, and agent skills, so an orchestrator can search approved capabilities at runtime instead of compiling every tool in at build time. This walkthrough shows the discover, instantiate, and execute loop in a working sample, with search results that return connection metadata but never invocation credentials. Tokenomics for coding agents: benchmark cost and quality on your own code – Coding assistants replay a growing transcript on every turn, so their cost math is nothing like ordinary inference. This post gives you open source tooling to measure model, harness, and hosting choices on your own repositories and build a cost-and-quality frontier you own, with sample results where routing came out 44.7 percent cheaper for 4.8 percent lower mean quality. How U.S. Bank migrated 119 TB from Oracle Exadata to Amazon RDS for Oracle – U.S. Bank moved four Oracle Exadata databases totaling about 119 TB to Amazon RDS for Oracle using a config-driven pipeline built on Oracle XTTS, AWS DataSync, and Amazon EFS. The initial baseline copy finished in about 7 days with zero data loss and cutovers averaging roughly four hours per database, over a bandwidth-capped Direct Connect link. Upcoming AWS events Mark your calendars for these upcoming events. AWS re:Invent – AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas, with more than 2,200 sessions. The session catalog is live and reserved seating is open, so now is the time to build your schedule. AWS Community Days – AWS Community Day Brasil Norte takes place in Belém on October 31, closing out the 2026 Brazilian community season. Check the hub for events near you. That’s all for this week. Check back next Monday for another Weekly Roundup! – Daniel This post is part of our Weekly Roundup series. Check back each week for a quick roundup of interesting news and announcements from AWS!

Google is working with a company called Ignite to use AI and satellite data to map remote homes and plan the best delivery routes for solar panels. Subscribe Across sub-Saharan Africa, nearly half the continent’s population — over 600 million people — live without electricity. Families rely on costly kerosene and candles for basic lighting to study, do chores, or move safely around the home. Off-grid solar power offers one of the cleanest and fastest ways to bridge this gap. In order to reach millions of dispersed households with this technology, we must solve three critical challenges: locating unmapped homes without formal addresses, navigating difficult rural terrain to deliver solar hardware, and identifying installations remotely despite the limits of satellite imagery. To help on-the-ground climate innovators solve data and logistical barriers beyond our own operational footprint, Google spent the past three years collaborating with Ignite Energy Access through our Startups for Sustainable Development program. An off-grid clean energy pioneer aiming to connect 100 million people throughout Africa to electricity by 2030 Ignite worked alongside Google researchers, engineers, and data specialists across more than 100 dedicated advisory sessions,to transform these logistical roadblocks into a repeatable blueprint for expanding energy access. Solving last-mile logistics Most rural communities are only connected by unmapped dirt paths across rugged terrain. To expand access to off-grid solar, the first step is pinpointing households that need it, and these homes don’t appear in standard mapping apps. To locate these, our joint team combined satellite imagery and Google’s Open Buildings dataset with smart routing algorithms. The field teams then need to reach these remote households. Google researchers are developing advanced geospatial models that identify rural paths and incorporate them into real-world routing constraints. Google's Operations Research (OR) models are helping to optimize Ignite’s end-to-end supply chain. By evaluating potential network configurations, the system identifies where central warehouses and local mini-hubs should go while carefully balancing operational constraints such as transportation costs, delivery routes, vehicle capacities, and inventory holding expenses. Scaling electrification from space As electrification ramps up across Africa, operators need to know where micro-solar systems (usually consisting of a single rooftop panel) are already active. Mapping these installations allows teams to identify underserved villages, deploy resources strategically, and plan future rollouts. However, standard satellite imagery only registers a single rooftop panel as barely one pixel, so visual targeting is nearly impossible at scale. To solve this, Google researchers are developing computer vision models using Gemini for Science and fine-tuning them with ground-truth drone imagery provided by Ignite to map solar setups from orbit. The team is testing thousands of code variations to increase precision and recall rates, turning satellite data into a strategic compass for future clean-energy deployment. Transforming local economies Together, what began as a set of isolated friction points — unmapped dirt paths and single-pixel satellite signatures — is evolving into a playbook for expanding energy access while cutting emissions in emerging markets worldwide. The environmental impact is already measurable: In the first half of 2026 alone, we estimate our partnership with Ignite Energy Access has enabled over 160,000 tCO2e in emissions reductions, driven by 3.7 million solar devices delivered across the region since 2023. 1 These milestones bring us closer to Google’s aspiration to help partners collectively reduce one gigaton of carbon-equivalent emissions annually by 2030. Laying the groundwork Google and Ignite are already preparing for the next phase in the energy transition: clean cooking. Millions of rural families still rely on wood and charcoal for meals, filling homes with harmful smoke and requiring hours of daily fuel collection, a burden disproportionately affecting women and girls. Modern electric cookstoves eliminate these indoor toxins, but they require far more power than what an individual rooftop solar kit can generate. To address this challenge, our partnership is modeling community-level micro-grids capable of delivering the energy required to power clean electric cooking. The goal is a comprehensive energy system that not only lights rural homes, but also protects family health and drives down household emissions. title: We’re helping farmers around the world connect to essential services online.
body: We’re helping farmers around the world connect to essential services online. Rowan Barnett Director Google.org, APAC, EMEA & Global Stronger Communities Oct 26, 2026 Under the World Bank Group’s AgriConnect initiative, Google.org is supporting the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and broader World Bank Group (WBG) to better empower farmers . Their collective goal is to help 1 million farmers access crucial livelihood-improving services by the end of 2027. With Google.org’s $2.5 million in support, the WBG will expand digital public infrastructure (DPI) for agriculture: shared digital systems that act as “public roads” for online services. Following a successful pilot in India, the WBG will build an AI-enabled Open Network for Agriculture (ONA) across several countries spanning Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. By connecting public and private sector service providers in a shared digital network, ONA lets farmers avoid separate, disconnected apps, using a single platform to access vital resources like digital farmer IDs, credit lines, direct subsidy payments, markets to sell produce, and voice-powered advice in their local language on farming, weather, pricing, and finances. This support builds on an alliance between Google and the World Bank Group to accelerate digital transformation in emerging markets.
retained_feed_body: Google.org is investing $2.5M to help 1 million farmers access AI-powered agricultural services via the World Bank's ONA. See how it works.

title: How Google Beam connects military families globally
body: How Google Beam connects military families globally Oct 26, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Together with the USO, we are bringing Google Beam to 20 locations globally so deployed service members can experience lifelike, 3D video connections with their loved ones. Watch our new docuseries to see how four military families are staying connected, despite being miles apart. Josh Woodward VP, Google Labs, Gemini, & AI Studio Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary Google is partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 locations worldwide. This 3D video technology helps deployed service members feel truly present with their families by capturing lifelike body language and eye contact. You can watch the new docuseries to see how this tool bridges the distance for military families and visit the Google Beam website to learn more. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. "How Google Beam connects military families globally" shows how tech bridges the distance for soldiers. Google is partnering with the USO to bring 3D video communication to 20 locations. This lifelike technology helps families share milestones, like first steps and promotions, in real time. It captures body language and eye contact, making long-distance chats feel much more personal. You can watch a new docuseries to see how these reunions impact military families. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Google Beam uses AI to create lifelike 3D video calls that make it feel like you’re sitting right across from someone. Google is partnering with the USO to bring this tech to military families stationed far apart. It helps soldiers stay connected to their loved ones by capturing real-time body language and eye contact. This makes missing big moments, like a child’s first steps, feel a lot less lonely. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer For deployed service members, the hardest distance is measured in missed moments. A child’s first steps, a first performance, or simply sitting across the table from a loved one feels out of reach. That's why we’re partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 USO locations globally, helping service members bridge this distance. With Beam’s unique true-to-life, 3D video communication experience, families feel like they’re stepping into the same room and connecting in a whole new way. Google Beam began a pilot program connecting families between Trzebień, Poland, and Fort Bliss, Texas earlier this year. Now, we’re releasing a docuseries that shows how the program is expanding to Grafenwöhr, Germany, and Fort Hood, Texas, bringing this lifelike closeness to even more families. Directed by military veteran and filmmaker Kyle Hausmann-Stokes, our new docuseries captures the power of this connection. It follows four soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, 37th Armored Regiment (Iron Dukes) during their deployment in Poland. Watch the profound emotional impact of Google Beam as they reconnect with their families back home, proving that love knows no distance. Four families, one shared mission The Brown-Orane family Sergeant Amoy Brown is a Bradley Gunner deployed in Poland, and Tiyanna Orane, his wife, is an aviation logistics specialist in Fort Bliss. For them, military service is an equal partnership. But an eight-hour time difference makes celebrating major milestones,like Tiyanna’s military promotion, feel distant. Google Beam helped create an intimate, lifelike reunion where Amoy and Tiyanna could celebrate her achievement, and Amoy could interact with their young son, Azeal. The Kassales family Throughout his first two years of service, Army Chaplain Roland Kassales has been deployed for 15 months. Staying present with this family during the time apart is incredibly important. Google Beam helped bridge the distance, bringing his family into focus. When his daughter, Blythe, read stories she wrote to him aloud, Beam let him experience those moments in real time with the body language, eye contact, and all. The Jennings family Mayra Jennings manages a bustling, blended household of seven while working 12-hour work shifts, leaving her deployed husband, Sergeant First Class Matthew Jennings, feeling the absence of daily family life. Standard phone calls made it difficult to connect across the miles with their 4-year-old son, Dimitri, their newborn daughter, Lilly, and his two sisters. Google Beam gave Matthew a front-row seat to experience how much his newborn daughter had grown, to see one of his sisters play guitar, and offered Mayra a moment of comfort, recreating the feeling and warmth of sitting directly across the table from one another. The Rodriguez family Major Michael Rodriguez, an armor battalion operations officer with 12 years of service, knows the heavy toll deployments take, especially on his family. His wife Jessica balances a demanding job as a pediatric physical therapist, while solo parenting their four young children. With Google Beam they’re able to create new memories, including witnessing his one-year-old daughter Kathryn practice taking her first steps. Watch the docuseries To see these emotional reunions and follow the journey of the Brown, Kassales, Jennings, and Rodriguez families, watch the complete docuseries . And to learn more about how Beam is redefining human connection visit goo.gle/USO . title: D.C. Man Arrested for Murdering Two Youths, Ages 12 and 14
body: Press Release D.C. Man Arrested for Murdering Two Youths, Ages 12 and 14 Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – Antonio Terry, 18, of Washington, D.C., was arrested on October 25, 2026, and charged today with first-degree murder while armed for the shooting deaths of two youths, ages 12 and 14, that occurred on April 14, 2026, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Judge Heide Hermann found probable cause that Terry committed the offense of first-degree murder while armed and ordered that Terry be held without bond pending a preliminary hearing scheduled for November 9, 2026. According to court documents, at approximately 3:27 p.m., on April 14, 2026, a stolen, black Honda Accord drove up to the entrance of the parking lot to the Circle 7 Express store 740 Kenilworth Avenue, Northeast. Three masked males got out of the car, opened fire on individuals in the parking lot, and then returned to the car and fled the scene. Two youths, ages 12 and 14 were shot and killed. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. This case is being investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Christopher Carson and Yasmin Emrani. These charges are merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 26, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Federal Jury Convicts Child Sex Trafficker on All Charges
body: Press Release Federal Jury Convicts Child Sex Trafficker on All Charges Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Indiana INDIANAPOLIS- A federal jury has found Jacquez “Joc” Brown, 31, of Chicago, guilty of Sex Trafficking of a Minor, Sexual Exploitation of a Child, and three counts of Distribution of Child Sexual Abuse Material. The verdict was returned on October 15, 2026, following a three-day trial. According to court documents and evidence introduced at trial, on December 14, 2022, Vigo County 911 received an emergency text message reporting that a 15-year-old female was being prostituted by a 28-year-old male, later identified as Brown, at the Super 8 Motel in Terre Haute. Terre Haute Police Department (THPD) officers located the minor victim in a motel room with Brown. The subsequent investigation revealed that Brown compelled the minor to engage in commercial sex acts for his financial benefit and had taken a sexually explicit photograph of her during the trafficking that he sent to numerous individuals to entice them to pay for sex with the minor victim. Investigators also found multiple advertisements depicting the minor victim that included nude photographs of the victim and a phone number associated with Brown. Despite police intervention on December 14, Brown continued arranging commercial sex acts involving the minor. The jury received testimony from law enforcement officers who encountered Brown and the minor victim; reviewed text message exchanges that demonstrated the trafficking activity as it occurred; heard from a digital forensic expert who conclusively linked Brown to the creation and transmission of those messages and to the device used to capture and distribute the illicit image; and listened to first‑hand accounts of the sex‑trafficking conduct from friends and associates of Brown and the minor victim who personally experienced the events. Homeland Security Investigations and Terre Haute Police Department investigated this case. Chief U.S. District Judge James R. Sweeney, II presided over the trial and will determine Brown’s sentence at a later date. U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys, Carolyn Haney and MaryAnn Mindrum, who are prosecuting this case. ### Updated October 26, 2026 Topics Project Safe Childhood Human Trafficking Component USAO - Indiana, Southern

title: Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison for Coercion and Enticement of a Minor and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison for Coercion and Enticement of a Minor and Receipt of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of New York Defendant Had Two Prior New York State Convictions for Sexually Assaulting Children Joseph Grunwald was sentenced yesterday by United States District Judge Nina R. Morrison to 30 years’ imprisonment for coercing and enticing a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct, and receiving child pornography. The sentencing was held on October 22, 2026.  Grunwald pleaded guilty to a three-count superseding information in August 2026. Grunwald was a registered sex offender in New York State when he committed the federal crimes of conviction. Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the sentence. “The defendant has demonstrated that he poses a grave danger to children. Today’s sentence was necessary to protect the community from this recidivist menace for decades,” stated United States Attorney Nocella.  “Notably, the defendant’s prior New York State sentences for sexually assaulting minors – in each case, he received probation – failed to deter him.” “While nothing can undo the harm suffered by the victims, this significant sentence ensures Joseph Grunwald, a convicted sex offender, will spend the next three decades unable to victimize additional children.  The FBI/NYPD Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force works day in and day out to hold accountable those who prey on children.  Individuals who choose to target the most vulnerable should take note: justice will find you,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. As set forth in court filings, between March 2023 and December 2023, Grunwald communicated over the internet and through social media with two children, John Doe-1, a 14-year-old boy, and John Doe-2, another minor boy, soliciting them both for sexually explicit videos and images.  Grunwald first contacted John Doe-1 on the messaging app Telegram, confirmed that the victim was a minor, and solicited a sexually explicit picture from him.  Grunwald was 31 years old at the time.  John Doe-1 later learned that the defendant had sent the sexually explicit picture, without the victim’s knowledge, to a group chat.  In June 2023, Grunwald began threatening the victim.  For example, on June 26, the defendant threatened:  “You’re still in trouble and remember what I said yesterday. Those boys told me something about you.”  The following day, on June 27, the defendant threatened John Doe-1 again after chasing him though the boy’s synagogue: “I am going to call your mother.  I have her cell phone number.  Good luck.  I’m going to tell her everything.” Grunwald also solicited sexually explicit pictures from John Doe-2, exchanging thousands of messages with the victim on Instagram.  Grunwald confirmed John Doe-2 was a minor, but later falsely told John Doe-2 that Grunwald was 18-years-old.  Law enforcement also seized multiple electronic devices from Grunwald containing additional child pornography in the form of pictures and videos of other minors. Grunwald was previously convicted in 2019 of sexually abusing a 7-year-old girl in a synagogue, and was sentenced to 10 years’ probation.  While the charges in that case were still pending, Grunwald sexually abused a 13-year-old boy in exchange for a cell phone and the use of the defendant’s debit card.  He pleaded guilty to misdemeanor sexual abuse and was sentenced to three years’ probation. This prosecution is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse.  Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.  For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s General Crimes Section. Assistant U.S. Attorney Vincent Chiappini is in charge of the prosecution. The Defendant : JOSEPH GRUNWALD Age:  34 Brooklyn, New York. E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 24-CR-19 (NRM) Contact John Marzulli Denise Taylor United States Attorney’s Office (718) 254-6323 Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Eastern

title: Canton Man Found Guilty of Child Exploitation Offense and Receipt of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Canton Man Found Guilty of Child Exploitation Offense and Receipt of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Robert Bowen, age 46, of Canton, New York, has been found guilty of sexual exploitation of a child and receipt of child pornography following a bench trial in Syracuse. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone made the announcement. Evidence presented during the bench trial proved that, in June 2025, Bowen exchanged text messages with an 8-year-old child using the Roblox application and later using his cell phone’s messaging application.  During the exchange, Bowen sent the child pornographic media and requested the child take sexually explicit images and videos of herself and send them to Bowen.  The evidence established that Bowen received sexually explicit media from the child, and requested she send more. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “Bowen used an online gaming platform, frequently visited by children to encounter and prey upon an innocent victim. Fortunately, the child’s family reported the conduct to police and Bowen was swiftly identified, thanks to the investigative efforts and successful partnership between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. I encourage parents and guardians to be vigilant about who their children are communicating with online. My office remains committed to protecting our communities against Internet predators such as the defendant.” “Robert Bowen’s conduct reflects the disturbing and reprehensible lengths to which some individuals will go to prey upon and exploit the most vulnerable among us” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony J. Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “The exploitation of even one child is unacceptable and demands an unwavering and coordinated response. HSI Massena remains resolute in its commitment to working with our law enforcement partners across state lines to identify, apprehend and hold accountable those who harm children.” Bowen will be sentenced on February 11, 2027, by Chief United States District Judge Brenda K. Sannes, who presided over the bench trial and rendered the guilty verdicts.  The sexual exploitation of a child charge against Bowen carries a maximum sentence of 30 years in prison, a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  The defendant will also be required to register as a sex offender.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the statutes the defendant violated, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, and other factors. Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case, with assistance from the New York State Police and the Lombard, Illinois, Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ben Gillis and Tamara Thomson are prosecuting the case. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

Courcelle. According to the indictment, on April 1, 2026, WILTZ was convicted of multiple felonies in Orleans Parish, including illegal possession of stolen things valued over $25,000. Less than two months later, on May 28, 2026, WILTZ was arrested in possession of a Glock Model 19 firearm and additional ammunition. As to both offenses, WILTZ faces up to 15 years in prison, up to a $250,000 fine, and up to three years of supervised release. Each count also carries a mandatory $100 special assessment fee. U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely an allegation and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and Louisiana Probation and Parole. Assistant United States Attorney David Berman of the Violent Crime Unit is in charge of the prosecution. title: Oneida County Man Pleads Guilty to Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Oneida County Man Pleads Guilty to Possession of Child Pornography Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Jeffrey Schreck, age 63, of Utica, New York, pled guilty today to possessing child pornography announced First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). As part of his guilty plea, Schreck admitted that in December of 1997, he was convicted under New York state law of two counts of sodomy in the second degree. The convictions stemmed from Schreck’s sexual abuse of an eleven-year-old female child. Schreck also admitted that in February of 2026, he possessed a cell phone and a tablet on which Schreck possessed numerous images and videos of child pornography, including material depicting the sexual abuse of children as young as two years old. Due to Schreck’s prior New York state conviction, at sentencing, Schreck faces a mandatory minimum term of 10 years in federal prison and a statutory maximum of 20 years. Schreck also faces a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  Schreck will also be required to register as a sex offender upon his release from prison. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. Sentencing is currently scheduled for February 5, 2027, at 11:00 am in Syracuse, New York, before Chief U.S. District Judge, Brenda K. Sannes. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “This defendant’s recidivism has landed him back in jail, this time, for 10 to 20 years. Our priority is to find and prosecute anyone who victimizes children whether that be through hands-on abuse or through the trafficking and possession of child pornography. Our children deserve to be protected and we remain dedicated, as do our law enforcement partners, to doing whatever we can to ensure they are.” “This defendant’s prior conviction for sexually abusing a child and his subsequent possession of child sexual abuse material demonstrate the ongoing danger posed by repeat offenders,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “HSI Syracuse is committed to holding repeat offenders accountable, protecting the most vulnerable members of our communities, and ensuring that those who exploit children face the full consequences of their actions.” HSI is investigating the case with assistance from the New York State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jessica Carbone and Adrian LaRochelle are prosecuting the case as a part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. title: U.S. Attorney’s Office announces 2026 Election Integrity Plan for general election and early voting in Kansas
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office announces 2026 Election Integrity Plan for general election and early voting in Kansas Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas KANSAS CITY, KAN. – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Kansas (USAO-KS), in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , unveils its comprehensive strategy to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting begins in Kansas for the 2026 midterm elections . “President Abraham Lincoln said it best when he said we are a ‘government of the people, by the people, for the people’,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “Voting gives American citizens a voice in their government, and fair elections are the heart of our democratic republic. Our office will work to ensure that Kansans can cast their ballots without fear or worry that voting results will be tainted by fraud, intimidation, or illegal ballots.” The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements. Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: • Protecting Voter Rights : Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. • Ensuring Voter Eligibility and Enforcement : Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources. • Combating Election Fraud : Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. Mail-In and Early Voting in Kansas Kansas state election officials have confirmed that early in-person voting and mail-in voting have begun. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered. Reporting Election Irregularities Assistant U.S. Attorney/District Election Officer Jared Maag will be on duty in this District while the polls are open. He can be reached by the public at (785) 295-2850. The public plays a critical role in maintaining election security. Anyone who witnesses or has direct knowledge of potential election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity is strongly encouraged to report it immediately. You can also visit the official FBI Tips Portal to report potential election fraud or voting irregularities. Complaints regarding voter discrimination or civil rights violations can also be directed to the Civil Rights Division via the Department of Justice Civil Rights Reporting Portal . Please note, however, in the case of a crime of violence or intimidation, call 911 immediately and before contacting federal authorities. State and local police have primary jurisdiction over polling places, and almost always have faster reaction capacity in an emergency. ### Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Kansas

title: Syracuse Man Charged with Making Threats Against the President
body: Press Release Syracuse Man Charged with Making Threats Against the President Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Christopher Vignogna, age 26, of Syracuse, New York, appeared in Federal Court Friday, October 9, 2026, on a charge of making threats against the President of the United States. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and United States Secret Service, Special Agent in Charge Charles T. Perras made the announcement. The complaint filed against Vignogna alleges that on October 7, 2026, Vignogna asked a co-worker to inquire if her boyfriend could buy Vignogna a gun so he could shoot the President at a rally in Syracuse on October 9, 2026.  The complaint alleges that Vignogna also stated that Trump is coming to Syracuse and I want to shoot him. The charge filed against Vignogna carries a maximum sentence of 5 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of up to 3 years.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. Vignogna was arraigned before United States Magistrate Judge Mitchell J. Katz and released on conditions pending a trial. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “I want to commend the U.S. Secret Service for their swift and immediate response to this serious conduct.  May this arrest serve as a deterrent to others who think it is acceptable to threaten the President of the United States.  It will not be tolerated on my watch.” United States Secret Service, Special Agent in Charge Charles T. Perras said, “The United States Secret Service reaffirms that the safety and security of our protectees remains our highest priority. Every potential threat is taken seriously, investigated thoroughly, and pursued with the full intention of bringing individuals who violate the law to justice.  This mission is not accomplished alone. Collaboration with our state, local, and federal partners is essential to ensuring swift and successful protective and investigative operations. The Secret Service extends its appreciation to the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Northern District of New York, the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Office, and the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office for their continued support and cooperation.” The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. This case is being investigated by the United States Secret Service. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Whalen. Updated October 26, 2026 Topic National Security Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Broome County Trio Arrested in Large Scale Meth Ring
body: Press Release Broome County Trio Arrested in Large Scale Meth Ring Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On October 2, 2026, Jermaine Cooper, age 53, of Apalachin, NY; Sherry Olk, age 40, of Binghamton, NY; and Shamell Tate, age 36 of Endicott, NY, were arraigned on charges of distribution of methamphetamine. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, FBI Special Agent in Charge Craig Tremaroli, Broome County District Attorney F. Paul Battisti, Broome County Sheriff Frederick J. Akshar II, New York State Police (NYSP) Bureau of Criminal Investigation Lieutenant Nate McCarthy, and Vestal Police Chief Vince Stavola made the announcement. The complaint against Cooper and Olk, alleges the two sold over 100 grams of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine in July 2026.  A separate complaint against Tate alleges in September 2026, he sold over 200 grams of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine. These charges carry a mandatory minimum sentence of 5 years in prison, a maximum sentence of 40 years in prison, a fine up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. All defendants are currently detaining pending a trial before a United States District Court. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “These three drug dealers have been exploiting drug addiction for their financial gain and infiltrating deadly narcotics into our community for far too long. New York’s bail reform laws would have allowed these defendants right back on the street after arraignment, and my office will continue to use federal laws to remove drug traffickers from the community and safeguard the Southern Tier. These arrests should serve as a chilly reminder that if you are poisoning our communities with narcotics, we will find you and bring the fullest extent of the federal government to your doorstep.” “These arrests and seizures are a direct result of the continued partnerships and incredible coordination we share at every level of law enforcement throughout Broome County,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “As alleged, these subjects were making a living off bringing dangerous drugs into our communities, not caring how it was hurting our neighbors. But law enforcement cares, and now they are all facing potential time in federal prison. The FBI remains deeply committed to working with our partner agencies to aggressively investigate drug traffickers and ensure they are sent to prison.” Broome County District Attorney Paul Battisti stated, “This coordinated effort demonstrates the effectiveness of multi-agency collaboration in tackling drug-related crimes. No longer are the days of federal, state and local law enforcement agencies working in silos. As has been demonstrated with Clean Sweep in April and again today with Cold Front, we are One Team, laser focused on the safety and security of our community and will stop at nothing when public safety is at risk.” “Getting dangerous drug dealers off our streets is what the law-abiding residents and families of our community expect and deserve from law enforcement,” said Broome County Sheriff Fred Akshar.  “It takes coordination, cooperation and teamwork at every level to build a safer Broome County and to put the peddlers of poison where they belong, behind bars and unable to create new victims.” NYSP Bureau of Criminal Investigation Lieutenant Nate McCarthy stated, “I would like to thank all of the law enforcement professional that touched this case, including many of our agencies’ civilian support staff.  Each member contributed to this investigation, leading to its success. These cases demand extensive investigative expertise, coordination, and countless hours of work.  The results speak for themselves and are a direct reflection of the commitment and strength of our continued partnerships.” Vestel Police Chief Vince Stavola stated, “This case reinforces that effective interagency partnerships are essential to addressing public safety and protecting the communities we serve. By sharing resources, maintaining open lines of communication, and working toward a common goal, we can collectively achieve better outcomes and improve public safety not only in the Town of Vestal, but throughout our surrounding communities.” The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. FBI, NYSP, Broome County Sheriff’s Office and Vestal Police Department are investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kristen Grabowski and Michael Whalen are prosecuting the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the centerpiece of the Department of Justice’s violent crime reduction efforts.  PSN is an evidence-based program proven to be effective at reducing violent crime.  Through PSN, a broad spectrum of stakeholders work together to identify the most pressing violent crime problems in the community and develop comprehensive solutions to address them.  As part of this strategy, PSN focuses enforcement efforts on the most violent offenders and partners with locally based prevention and reentry programs for lasting reductions in crime. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psn . Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Fayetteville Drug Dealer Sentenced to 17 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Fayetteville Drug Dealer Sentenced to 17 Years in Federal Prison Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of North Carolina USANCE.PublicInfoOfficer@usdoj.gov NEW BERN, N.C. – A federal judge sentenced Donquel Caron McEachern, 36, of Fayetteville, to over 17 years in federal prison for selling cocaine and fentanyl throughout Cumberland County. On June 18, 2026, McEachern pleaded guilty to conspiring to distribute 400 grams of fentanyl, over 1 pound of cocaine, 28 grams of crack cocaine, and marijuana. He also admitted possessing 400 grams of fentanyl, over 1 pound of cocaine, and 28 grams of crack cocaine with the intent to distribute, as well as possessing a gun to assist his drug selling. “McEachern built a drug selling business that pumped fentanyl, cocaine, and other deadly poison into Cumberland County while menacing folks with his guns at every turn,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “His blind greed endangered families, fueled addiction, and showed a blatant disregard for the safety of this community. Today’s sentence reflects the gravity of his actions and our continued commitment to dismantling the organizations and individuals who profit from spreading this poison. Simple lesson; drugs kill, prison awaits, do better.” In 2023, law enforcement began investigating McEachern as a major drug supplier of fentanyl, cocaine, and other narcotics in Fayetteville. That same year, officers twice found him in possession of cocaine and a firearm. After those encounters, investigators determined that McEachern and members of his drug trafficking organization used Airbnb rentals as “trap houses” to store, prepare, package, and distribute drugs. On November 6, 2024, investigators executed a search warrant at one of the Airbnb McEachern used. Inside, they found approximately 5 pounds of cocaine, 2 pounds of fentanyl, 53 grams of crack cocaine, five guns, and body armor. McEachern just picked up and moved to a new location to continue selling drugs. During two more separate traffic stops leading up to May 2025, investigators found him with three guns and thousands of dollars in cash. On May 1, 2025, law enforcement executed two additional search warrants at the new Airbnb rentals he used for drug distribution and seized more guns, fentanyl, cocaine, and drug‑trafficking paraphernalia. “This sentencing demonstrates what can be accomplished when law enforcement agencies work together through the Homeland Security Task Force,” said Michael J. Connolly, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Atlanta Field Division. “By combining our expertise and resources, we are strengthening our efforts to dismantle criminal networks, disrupt drug trafficking, and protect the communities we serve.” "The Fayetteville Police Department is dedicated to maximizing our federal partnerships to target and dismantle those who exploit drug addiction for personal gain. The conviction and federal sentencing of McEachern demonstrate the decisive impact of collaborative enforcement across federal, state, and local agencies. Let this serve as a stern warning to anyone distributing illegal drugs in our city; you will be held fully accountable under the law." This prosecution is part of Operation Gate Keeper, a component of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) established under Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole‑of‑government initiative committed to dismantling criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking networks operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Charlotte comprises agents and officers from the DEA, ATF, FBI, HSI, Fayetteville Police Department, and Hope Mills Police Department with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of North Carolina. W. Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, made the announcement following sentencing by U.S. District Judge Louise W. Flanagan. The DEA, Fayetteville Police Department, and Hope Mills Police Department investigated the case. A copy of this press release is available on our website . Related court documents and additional information can be found at the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:25-CR-205-FL-1. title: Maryland Man Pleads Guilty to Burning Commercial Establishment
body: Press Release Maryland Man Pleads Guilty to Burning Commercial Establishment Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Greenbelt, Maryland – A Maryland man pled guilty to arson in federal court, today, stemming from an incident in which he set fire to a commercial building. Shawn Justice, 38, of Avenue, pled guilty to one count of arson. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty plea with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Chief Caroll H. Spriggs, II, Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal. According to his guilty plea, on October 29, 2025, Justice entered Pasha Lounge, a bar and Hookah establishment in Waldorf, Maryland, through the front door and went to a humidor.  Justice then went inside of the humidor where he scattered cigars on the ground, poured liquor over them, lit a paper towel roll on fire, and then tossed the flaming paper-towel roll on the floor littered with alcohol-soaked cigars.  The humidor burst into flames, resulting in the lounge incurring more than $80,000 in losses. Justice faces a maximum of 20 years in federal prison for arson.  U.S. District Judge Theodore J. Chuang scheduled sentencing for Friday, Mar. 5, 2027, at 2:30 p.m. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal for their work in the investigation. U.S. Attorney Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Alex Treiger who is prosecuting this case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 26, 2026 Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Maryland

title: Illegal Immigrant from Mexico Pleads Guilty to Staging Fake Kidnapping Last Year Purportedly Committed by Federal Agents
body: Press Release Illegal Immigrant from Mexico Pleads Guilty to Staging Fake Kidnapping Last Year Purportedly Committed by Federal Agents Monday, October 26, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California LOS ANGELES – An illegal alien from Mexico pleaded guilty today to orchestrating a phony kidnapping last year that she blamed on federal agents or people working with federal agents. Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón, 43, of South Los Angeles, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to impede, obstruct, impair, and defeat the lawful function of Homeland Security Investigations within federal jurisdiction. According to her plea agreement, in June 2025, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) was engaged in carrying out lawful government functions, including credible threats to public safety such as kidnapping. In June and July of 2025, Calderón faked her apprehension by federal agents or surrogates acting on behalf of federal agents. On June 25, 2025, Calderón falsely told an individual that “immigration” was taking her while in or near a fast-food restaurant and that immigration officials had “turned the lights on,” “threatened to break her window” and were taking her into custody, according to court documents. Two days later, Calderón called another individual, who was a member of a tenants’ rights group, using the caller ID blocking feature on her telephone and falsely claimed she had been taken by “authorities” to San Ysidro where Calderón and others were pressured to sign voluntary removal documents. That same day, Calderón called a third individual, again using the caller ID blocking feature on her phone, and falsely claimed that she had been moved to a warehouse in an unknown location where she was being held with other detainees. On June 28, 2025, Calderón made another phone call to the second individual she contacted, using her caller ID blocking phone feature, and said she was being held with someone from “B-18” (an immigration facility in Los Angeles) and another person who had been “picked up at a gas station in Bakersfield.” As a result of Calderón’s intentional lies, false information was reported to the media and law enforcement that Calderón had been “kidnapped” by masked men in plain clothes driving an unmarked vehicle, who were acting as federal agents or as surrogates of federal agents. On June 30, 2025, in Los Angeles, community organizers held a press conference where other individuals repeated Calderón’s lies and demanded her “release” from custody. Meanwhile, Calderón knew about the false media coverage and chose to stay hidden in Bakersfield. On July 3, 2025, Calderón used the caller ID blocking feature on her phone again called an individual and falsely claimed she would be released soon because of all the media coverage. That same day, she traveled from Bakersfield to Tulare County to stage her release from custody. She then approached an individual in Tulare County and lied that she had just been dropped off by “Border Patrol.” She then asked this individual to be a witness in her “case” against “Border Patrol” because she planned to sue that agency. Calderón also altered her appearance to make it appear that she had been mistreated while in custody. A co-conspirator took photographs of Calderón’s altered appearance. From July 3, 2025, to July 5, 2025, Calderón turned off her phones and refused to return the phone calls of law enforcement officials, and caused others to do the same, when she knew law enforcement was looking for her. Calderón knew or had reason to know that law enforcement would expend resources looking for her because of her false kidnapping claims. United States District Judge Stephen V. Wilson scheduled a February 8, 2027, sentencing hearing, at which time Calderón will face a statutory maximum sentence of five years in federal prison. HSI’s El Camino Real Financial Crimes Division, a multi-agency division of HSI Los Angeles that includes federal and state investigators, investigated this matter. Assistant United States Attorneys Lana Morton Owens of the National Security Division and Matthew J. Tako of the Transnational Organized Crime Section are prosecuting this case. Contact Ciaran McEvoy Public Information Officer ciaran.mcevoy@usdoj.gov (213) 894-4465 Updated October 26, 2026 Topic Immigration Component USAO - California, Central Press Release Number: 26-205
